caption:
AI test scores are shaky. The rankings aren't.

AI benchmarks are tests that score and rank models. But computer scientist Moritz Hardt says the scores themselves can mislead. Change a test set only slightly and you get completely different accuracy numbers. Say, 90% on one dataset and 73% on another.

The catch? Rankings have held up well. A model that beats another on one test tends to beat it on other datasets too. That only works when models train on the same data. With today's LLMs, we don't know what they were trained on, and builders can shape data to boost benchmark results.

The payoff? Hardt's idea is to let everyone prepare, like athletes who all train at altitude. The scores may be inflated, but the rankings can be restored.

Source: Quanta Magazine — He Wants AI Benchmarking To Be a Science, Not a Dark Art
